correctness.rationale: At height y, direct three branch formulas identify the horizontal transformation as first return to J_y of circle rotation by λ on length 1+λ; the deleted circular interval has length c=λ y/y*. For λ=p/q, the primitive rotation period N=p+q forms N equispaced points of gap 1/q. In a deletion of length (k+θ)/q the grid loses k or k+1 points with phase fractions 1-θ,θ, giving return periods N-k,N-k-1. Lebesgue sampling of starting points requires size weighting by retained orbit size, so horizontal lengths are (1-θ)(N-k)/q and θ(N-k-1)/q. Uniform c scaling with y integrates each height band to weights 1/2 at endpoints, 1 in middle; total area y*(2q+p)/(2q) yields exact formula, with y* canceling all angles. Irrational rigid rotation and its induced interval exchange prove minimal/unique ergodic on each slice. Independent rational algebra checks p/q=1/2,2/5,3/7,4/9,5/11, including 2/5 fractions 7/24,1/2,5/24. These examples are not the all-p,q proof.

final_claim: For a three-cone zero-rotation translated-cone exchange with reduced λ=p/q in (0,1), the invariant interpolation trapezium has least periods q,q+1,...,p+q with normalized planar areas 2(p+q-j)w_j/[p(2q+p)] at period p+q-j, half endpoint weights w0=wp=1/2 and unit interior weights, independent of cone angles; irrational horizontal slices are aperiodic and equidistributed.
limitations: Only zero-rotation three-cone invariant interpolation trapezium, normalized two-dimensional Lebesgue area, 0<λ<1.
The irrational result is equidistribution along each fixed-height horizontal slice, not across the full region.
